the continuance of something and its passing/running on

"he came to us after a sawʿ / suwāʿ of the night,"
the pouring out of something
māʾ thajjāj is water that pours out abundantly.
"May Umm ʿAmr be watered at the end of every night by dark rain-clouds whose water is a downpour (thajīj)."

A ḥadīth says: "The best ḥajj is al-ʿajj and al-thajj." Ibn Fāris explains al-ʿajj as raising the voice in the talbiyah (the call labbayka), and al-thajj as the flowing of the blood of the hady (the offering animals).
weighing something down with something else
she is called maw'ūda because, once buried alive, she is weighed down by the earth piled over her
gathering something in, enclosing or containing it
"I took in / held the knowledge."
"I packed the goods into the vessel."
"and evil is the foulest thing you have stowed away as provision."
relying on someone else in your own affair
an affair is entrusted (yūkal) to him.
